Today's big story: Will 2027 Be A 2022 Repeat For Stocks?

If you have watched Dell Technologies (DELL) stock fall over the past two months, you may wonder whether to buy or stay away. The shares closed at $312.54 on November 19, 2026, down 37.7% from $501.96 on October 27. They had closed at $587.59 on September 17, their high of the past year. The steepest drop hit on November 5, when the shares fell 14.9%. A decline of that speed can signal either a bargain or a warning. So how has Dell stock done after a fall like this before?

How Has Dell Stock Done After Past Falls?

Dell stock has fallen this hard and had a full year to recover only once before. Since December 2018, the shares have dropped more than 40% within 30 trading days just twice. The current decline crossed that mark on November 5, 2026, and remains too recent to evaluate. The first instance occurred on March 18, 2020, and a year later the shares were up 205%.

Dell's 205% gain after 2020 came from just one past fall. If a big part of your savings sits in Dell, that single good year is thin comfort after a 37.7% drop. Instead of one company, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio owns 30 quality companies in equal amounts, and it is up more than 105% since September 2020. Look inside HQ.

That 2020 buyer did not have to wait out any further declines. Dell never closed below its March 18 price in the twelve months that followed. Its highest price of that year arrived 364 days later, almost a full year on.

But the 2020 fall occurred alongside the whole market. Dell fell 43.4% in the 30 trading days to March 18, 2020, while an S&P 500 fund fell 27.0%. In the 30 trading days to the November 5, 2026 dip, Dell fell 40.8% while the same fund fell only 4.0%. This time, Dell has fallen almost alone.

Dell's Business Is Still Growing Under The Fall

Sales are growing quickly. Over the four fiscal quarters ended July 31, 2026, Dell's revenue reached $151 billion, up 49.0% from a year earlier. Its operating margin over that period rose to 9.6%, from 7.1% a year before. Management said on the September 1 call that Dell ended fiscal Q2 2027 with a record $95 billion of AI backlog, representing orders for AI servers still to be shipped.

title: What HPE Holders Should Watch In Monday's Margin
detail:
What HPE Holders Should Watch In Monday's Margin

Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Will 2027 Be A 2022 Repeat For Stocks?

Hewlett Packard Enterprise reports its fiscal fourth quarter on Monday, Nov 23, after the market close. Can HPE's AI servers lift its margin, or only its sales? The short answer is mixed. So far, HPE's margin has risen along with its sales. But HPE credits ordinary servers and networking for that, not AI servers. HPE itself expects AI servers to pull the margin back down.

Gross margin is the share of sales left after the direct cost of making the products. HPE's gross margin was 40.1% in the three months to July. A year earlier it was 29.2%. Revenue grew 33.7% over the same year.

AI servers were a small part of that. HPE's AI Systems revenue was almost $1.6 billion in the quarter. That is less than 13.1% of its revenue. HPE said the margin came from "disciplined pricing in traditional servers and increased networking mix".

We expect most previews to focus on AI server orders. This article looks at one number instead, the gross margin.

Where does HPE stock stand before the report?

HPE closed at $45.49 on Thursday. That is 38.1% below its Oct 9 close of $73.46, its highest of the past year. On Thursday, the S&P 500 fell 2.02%. HPE slipped 0.63%.

HPE now sits 38.1% under its October high, and Monday's report can move it again. If HPE is a big part of your savings, that is a fall you may have to sit through. When the market has fallen, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has lost about 81 cents for every $1 its benchmark lost, on average. See the HQ record.

The other AI hardware names have fallen further from their peak closes of the past year:

Dell Technologies is 46.9% below its Sep 17 record close.

Super Micro Computer is 52.5% below its June 2 high.

Nvidia, which makes the chips inside these servers, is 39.0% below its Oct 6 record close.

Did HPE's margin rise because of AI servers?

Not by HPE's own account. Its gross margin bottomed at 28.4% in the quarter to April 2025. It then rose in each of the next five quarters, to 40.1%. That is the highest of the 11 quarters Morningstar returns.

It is also well above HPE's normal level. Its gross margin averaged 33.1% a year from fiscal 2021 to 2025.

The server unit grew, but on price, not AI. HPE's Cloud & AI unit had $9 billion of revenue. HPE said higher prices for ordinary servers drove server revenue to an all-time high. The unit's operating margin, the share of sales left after all running costs, was 17%.

What does HPE expect AI servers to do to its margin?

HPE expects the margin to come down. It said gross margin should "moderate toward more historical levels". It named two causes, growth in AI systems and ordinary server margins returning to normal. More networking should partly offset that.

title: Why Is IBM (IBM) Down 11.2% Since Last Earnings Report?
detail:
Why Is IBM (IBM) Down 11.2% Since Last Earnings Report?
Zacks Equity Research
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 8:30 AM MST 5 min read
IBM
^GSPC
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

A month has gone by since the last earnings report for IBM (IBM). Shares have lost about 11.2% in that time frame, underperforming the S&P 500.

But investors have to be wondering, will the recent negative trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is IBM due for a breakout? Well, first let's take a quick look at its latest earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent catalysts for International Business Machines Corporation before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.

IBM Beats Q3 Earnings Estimates on Software, Infrastructure Growth

IBM reportedstrong third-quarter 2026 results, with adjusted earnings rising 11% year over year to $2.95 per share. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.88 by 2.4%. Revenues increased 4.7% to $17.10 billion, surpassing the consensus mark of $16.87 billion by 1.4%.

The upside reflected accelerating Software and Infrastructure growth, improved transaction execution and productivity initiatives. Software annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $24.9 billion, up 8% year over year. Operating pre-tax margin expanded 70 basis points (bps).

Software Growth Accelerates on Deal Closures

Software revenues increased 8.2% year over year to $7.80 billion, up 8.7% at constant currency. Hybrid Cloud revenues grew 11%, supported by Red Hat, while Data jumped 20% at constant currency, benefiting from Confluent's performance. Automation declined 3% amid a challenging comparison.

Transaction Processing rebounded sharply, growing 10% at constant currency after a soft prior quarter. Management attributed the recovery to renewed demand and the closure of approximately two-thirds of large transactions delayed from the second quarter. These deferred deals contributed roughly one-quarter of the sequential Software growth acceleration.

Red Hat bookings growth accelerated to the high teens, while OpenShift ARR surpassed $2.4 billion, increasing more than 30%. Software segment profit climbed 15.2% to $2.73 billion, lifting margin 210 bps to 35%.

Infrastructure Benefits From Storage Demand

Infrastructure revenues rose 4.2% year over year to $3.71 billion, representing 4.9% growth at constant currency. Hybrid Infrastructure advanced 9% at constant currency, driven by 32% growth in Distributed Infrastructure, reflecting broad-based strength in storage and Power systems.

IBM Z revenues declined 19% at constant currency against a demanding year-ago comparison. Nevertheless, the z17 program generated more than $1 billion in incremental revenues compared with the previous generation over six quarters. New midrange systems also delivered the platform's strongest midrange revenue launch in nearly two decades.

Infrastructure segment profit increased 11% to $715 million, while margin expanded 120 bps to 19.3%, aided by productivity initiatives.

Consulting Business Sees Modest Improvement

Consulting revenues were nearly flat year over year at $5.34 billion, increasing 1.8% at constant currency. Strategy and Technology grew 4% at constant currency, supported by application modernization and data and AI transformation demand. Intelligent Operations remained flat on a constant-currency basis.

Generative AI accounted for approximately 30% of quarterly Consulting revenues and 35% of backlog. Consulting signings totaled $5 billion, declining 2% at constant currency, while the trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio was 1.04.

Segment profit declined 4.8% to $653 million, with margin contracting around 60 bps to 12.2% as IBM reinvested productivity savings into digital capabilities.

Profitability Expands Despite Cost Pressure

IBM's non-GAAP gross profit rose 4% to $10 billion, although gross margin contracted 20 bps to 58.5%. Operating expenses and other income totaled $6.71 billion, increasing roughly 2% year over year.

Non-GAAP pre-tax income increased 9% to $3.30 billion, while adjusted EBITDA rose 7% to $4.9 billion. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved approximately 60 bps to 28.7%, reflecting operational efficiencies across general administration, sales and software development.

Strong Cash Flow and Liquidity

IBM generated $4.03 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter compared with $3.08 billion a year earlier. Free cash flow increased $0.7 billion to $3 billion. For the first nine months, free cash flow reached $7.8 billion, up $0.6 billion year over year.

The company exited the September quarter with $11.1 billion in cash, restricted cash and marketable securities. Total debt was $63.8 billion, including $12.7 billion attributable to IBM Financing. Quarterly dividend payments totaled approximately $1.6 billion.

Outlook

IBM reaffirmed its full-year 2026 constant-currency revenue growth expectation of 4% to 5%. However, management raised its free cash flow outlook, now anticipating an increase exceeding $1 billion year over year.

Software revenues are projected to grow 7% to 8%, supported by double-digit Hybrid Cloud growth and mid-teens Data expansion. Transaction Processing is now expected to remain flat for the year, an improvement from previous expectations.

Infrastructure revenues are forecast to grow in the low single digits, while Consulting growth is expected to accelerate to the low-to-mid-single-digit range. IBM also maintained its target of 100 bps operating pre-tax margin expansion for 2026, supported by continued productivity improvements.
